instruction: Arrange all transaction records by customer name in alphabetical order.

metadata.explanation: Task requires sorting all records by Customer column (column B) in alphabetical ascending order. Verified with Python: customers include Arnold Shawarma, Benedict Cucum, Bey Twice, and Blake Dreary. Evaluator extracts column B values and verifies they are sorted alphabetically.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts column B (Customer names) starting from row 2, matching the instruction requirement
Metric appropriately checks alphabetical sorting using Python's sorted() function
Postconfig properly saves the file before verification to ensure changes are persisted
Coverage is complete for the core requirement (alphabetical ordering of customer names)
Implementation handles edge cases well (None values, file retrieval, temp file cleanup)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The evaluator only verifies that column B is sorted, not that entire rows moved together during sorting. In practice this is fine (LibreOffice sort moves entire rows), but theoretically someone could manually reorder just column B values. Consider adding a check on another column if this edge case is a concern.

Minor: String sorting is case-sensitive by default. If customer names could have inconsistent capitalization, consider using case-insensitive comparison. Current implementation should work fine based on the actual data (properly capitalized names).
